Variable lookup order reversed causing incorrect values in stack traces

#### Description

When using stackprinter to format stack traces, variables are showing incorrect values due to the lookup order being reversed between local and global scopes.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import stackprinter

# Global variable
x = "global_value"

def test_function():
    # Local variable with same name
    x = "local_value"
    
    # This should show the local value but shows global instead
    msg = stackprinter.format()
    print(msg)

test_function()
```

The stack trace output shows `x = "global_value"` instead of the expected `x = "local_value"`. Local variables should take precedence over global variables when displaying variable values in stack traces, but the current behavior shows global values even when local variables exist with the same name.

This affects the accuracy of debugging information since developers expect to see the local variable values that are actually in scope at the point where the stack trace is generated.
